newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee market slows over holiday week.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee market slows over holiday week.

text.p: Vietnam's coffee trade has been quiet this week with little fluctuation in prices as the country marked a two-day national holiday, dealers said on Friday.
Robusta was quoted at between $1,360-$1,400 per tonne FOB Saigon Port on Friday, almost unchanged from last week.
Traders said prices were expected to follow recent increases on the London market once normal activity resumes.
Vietnam marked the 22nd anniversary of the Liberation of Saigon on Wednesday and Labour Day on Thursday.
Dealers questioned recent reports suggesting that as much as 40,000 tonnes of stock remains from Vietnam's 1996/97 harvest, saying the figure was likely to be much lower.
"I don't believe in this figure (40,000 tonnes), I think the stock that's left is about 25,000 tonnes only", one trader said. Others put the figure even lower.

An official at state coffee firm Vinacafe told Reuters on Friday that government approval had recently been given for the development of around 40,000 hectares (99,000 acres) of arabica coffee between now and the year 2001.

He said the project, aimed at northern and central areas of the country, would be funded by French development assistance and would target an eventual production capacity of around 44,000 tonnes each year.
Vietnam's 1996/97 robusta output has been estimated at 270,000 tonnes, representing an increase of around 60,000 tonnes from the previous harvest.
Current arabica production, for domestic consumption only, amounts to less than 10 percent of that total.
